name: Spinbutton
description: An input widget that restricts its value to a set or range of discrete values, featuring a text field with increase/decrease functionality via arrow keys.

optional_attributes.description: Human-readable value when numeric is not user-friendly
true when value is outside allowed range

notes: <input type='number'> is for QUANTITIES you would do arithmetic on. It is the wrong element for phone numbers, credit cards, postcodes, PINs or IDs — those are digit STRINGS. Use <input type='text' inputmode='numeric' pattern='[0-9]*'>.

Real problems with type='number': the scroll wheel silently changes the value when the page is scrolled with the field focused; non-numeric typed input is discarded with no feedback in some browsers; leading zeros are lost; and the spinner arrows are far below any reasonable target size.

Consider disabling the wheel: input.addEventListener('wheel', e => e.target === document.activeElement && e.preventDefault(), { passive: false }). An accidental scroll silently changing a quantity is a real data-integrity bug.
If you build custom +/- buttons, they need accessible names ('Increase quantity'), and the value must remain typeable in the input.
Custom +/- buttons should be tabindex='-1' when the input itself is focusable and arrows work — otherwise a 3-field form becomes 9 Tab stops. Keep them pointer targets.
Announce clamping (RAWeb 11.10): if the user types 999 and the max is 10, silently rewriting it to 10 is baffling. Say so.
role='spinbutton' on a div means you owe aria-valuenow/min/max, arrows, and typing. <input type='number'> already has all of it.
native_element: <input type="number"> — but read the notes; it is the wrong choice more often than people think

raweb_criteria.reason: The current value must be exposed; on a custom spinbutton, aria-valuenow/min/max are mandatory.
Up/Down arrows must change the value; the increment buttons must be keyboard reachable or explicitly excluded from the tab order in favour of the input.
It is a form field and needs a real label.
Visible focus indicator on the input.
Silently clamping or rejecting an out-of-range value is not error management — say what went wrong.
